# Thai-inspired neighborhood assets

Created 2026-09-24 with the built-in image_gen tool. Original PNGs preserved with real alpha transparency. Used by BazaarCityScene for street markets, shaded dining, a temple courtyard and connected shophouses. Sprite frames use JSON metadata; no source PNG pixels were edited locally.

## bazaar-street-life-v1.png

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent PNG atlas of SIX placeable everyday Thai-inspired neighborhood sprites for an existing top-down 16-bit JRPG. Square canvas in EXACTLY three columns and two rows, one independent sprite centered per equal cell, generous transparent gutters, no overlap. TOP LEFT: open fruit market stand, faded teal canvas awning over timber counter, baskets of green coconuts, yellow mangoes, bananas and green herbs. TOP MIDDLE: compact stainless steel noodle street-food pushcart with muted coral canvas sunshade, steaming stockpot, bowls, hanging utensils, no vendor. TOP RIGHT: small Thai open-sided sala shade pavilion, red and dark green tiled gable roof, modest gold finial, four wooden pillars and raised wooden bench, no deity. BOTTOM LEFT: cluster of three glazed ceramic and terracotta planters, lush banana leaves and tropical foliage. BOTTOM MIDDLE: neighborhood outdoor dining set, two small metal tables with bowls and six low colorful plastic stools, no people. BOTTOM RIGHT: freestanding Thai courtyard gate with white plaster pillars and compact ornate red-green tiled roof with slender gold finials, wide open passage, no wall extensions. Genuine transparent alpha around all objects. Coherent straight-on three-quarter TOP-DOWN JRPG perspective, front faces down, horizontal facades, no diamond isometric. Crisp pixel art, chunky nearest-neighbor clusters, approximately 48-96 logical pixel wide sprites, compact SNES style, warm daylight, weathered but cared-for everyday neighborhood, restrained terracotta teal cream ochre palette. No ground slabs, no scenery, no letters, no pseudo-script, no labels, no logos, no watermark, no Chinese red lanterns, no Japanese torii. Entire objects inside their own cells.

## bazaar-shophouse-row-v1.png

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single transparent building-block sprite for a top-down 16-bit JRPG, a Thai-inspired living neighborhood in a fictional tropical bazaar city. ONE connected row of THREE narrow two-story historic Bangkok-style shophouses sharing party walls, with a coherent roofline and street-facing ground-floor arcades. Weathered but lovingly maintained pastel pale yellow, muted pale turquoise and warm cream plaster facades; red-brown clay roof tiles, dark teak louvered shutters, carved timber balcony rails, small potted plants, modest external wiring and an air conditioner on one side, a few laundry cloths on a balcony. Ground floor: deep shaded open-front shops with muted green and terracotta retractable cloth awnings, woven baskets and rolled fabric by doorways, all blank signs. Everyday inhabited Thai streetscape, not palace, not fantasy European tavern. Three-quarter top-down classic JRPG view, all front walls face DOWN and align horizontally, roof viewed from above, NOT diamond isometric, no perspective vanishing point. Crisp pixel art with compact deliberate clusters and selective dark outlines, warm morning lighting, matching SNES-style characters around 48 pixels tall when the block is displayed 430 pixels wide. All buildings fully visible, generous transparent margin, genuine transparent alpha outside the block. Horizontal landscape image. No people, no vehicles, no ground slab, no streets or background, no text or fake lettering, no lanterns, no watermark.

The original shophouse image has transparent backdrop pixels despite the RGB background shown in some previews; its alpha was verified before integration. An unused background-removal variant was discarded because it contained a painted checkerboard.
